nodes.name: Hook frame and shared state
nodes.what: The shared frame every hook runs in: stdin parsing, crash log, paths, per-session state and the settings switches.
rules: A hook never imports another hook; shared code goes in hooks/lib/.
A hook's error never blocks the call: its outermost catch calls crashLog and it exits 0. The dispatcher's guards (guard: true) are the exception.
A refusal still exits 0: never let a hook's return value become its exit code (out and emit in hook-io.mjs).
Never save a state or JSON file with a bare fs.writeFileSync: go through state.mjs (its own .part file, rename with retries).
Never read a hook's switch only from process.env: settings env may not reach a hook process, so settings-env.mjs reads the files too.
Never compare or open a path from a tool input, the temp folder or a worktree without paths.mjs.

nodes.name: Hook texts and transcript reader
nodes.what: The strings hooks write and scanners match, plus the reader of Claude Code's transcript file and the Russian-language checks.
rules: A text one file writes and another greps for lives only in texts.mjs, so a reworded text cannot leave a scanner counting nothing.
The last section of texts.mjs is app text (Claude Code, Nimbalyst): never ours to change, only named there once.

nodes.name: Build and test gate
nodes.what: Stops a reply when code was edited and nothing was built or tested after it (a run of the project's verify skill counts). With --pre it checks each code commit with no verify run since the last code edit, in a project with a verify skill: logs it by default, refuses once with VERIFY_GATE_COMMIT=enforce.
rules: Never runs a command itself: it only asks for the build or test.
Block once is remembered in the hook's own state for each session, never by stop_hook_active alone (any Stop hook's block sets it).
Only the main session's edits count; a helper's brief carries its own check.

nodes.name: Reply-format gates
nodes.what: Hooks that check the reply before it goes out: links opened, file links clickable, and after the user stopped the session the next reply checked against the stop.
rules: Never refuse in the terminal: file-link-gate acts only under an app's CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT (sdk-...), the same test command-explain uses.
A link the user typed is never questioned by link-gate, and neither is a local or example address.

nodes.name: Helper brief gates
nodes.what: Checks on subagent calls: the systems map lines added to a brief (serves.mjs builds it), a helper that stopped cut or empty, and the read-only shell of the plan-reviewer and reviewer.
rules: A helper cut at its turn limit or with an empty report is never finished; a cut or empty reviewer counts as not run.
The reviewer and plan-reviewer never change a file: planner-readonly runs from those two agents' frontmatter only, with no entry in settings.json.

nodes.name: Shell command guards
nodes.what: Hooks that read a Bash or PowerShell command before it runs: explanation line, destructive SQL, bulk deletes, drive-wide searches, big downloads sent to the range downloader, read-only browser CLI, keys in a git push.
rules: The explanation line goes last, never first: Nimbalyst builds its Always allow rule from the command's first word, and a leading # would allow everything.
delete-guard, find-guard and sql-guard are the dispatcher's guards (guard: true): when one throws, cannot load or runs out of time, the call stops.
opencli-readonly lets only [read] site commands through: the person's signed-in accounts are never posted to, liked, followed or deleted from.
push-key-scan uses rules only: no model, no network.

nodes.name: Deep-research fence
nodes.what: A pre-tool hook that refuses a Workflow call named deep-research in an app or headless run (Nimbalyst, claude -p), where /deep-research skips its approval stop and can't be stopped; it says to run it in the terminal. Other workflows and the terminal pass.
rules: A guard of the dispatcher's pre-tool group (guard: true, tools: Workflow): when it throws, cannot load or runs out of time, only Workflow calls stop.
WORKFLOW_FENCE=off is read from the environment and from the env of settings.local.json or settings.json in ~/.claude only, not from a folder above home.

nodes.name: Nimbalyst tool gates
nodes.what: Hooks for Nimbalyst's own tools: a typing box on every question (the card first), pictures kept in the project, visible browser, session notes.
rules: Never fix a Nimbalyst tool call with updatedInput: the card keeps what Claude wrote, so the gate refuses or notes instead.
A picture is shown only from <project>/shown/, a folder nothing cleans up.
picture-gate is registered per project (quick-tasks), never globally.

nodes.name: Loop guard
nodes.what: repeat-guard stops looping inside one turn; wired with --near-cap-only, it only tells a helper near its turn cap to finish and report.
rules: Only the repeat-error part refuses; the same-file, same-call and near-cap parts never refuse.
Injected text (a background-task notice, a note) is not a new turn: it never resets the counts.

nodes.name: Session cleanup
nodes.what: A session closes what it started (dev servers, watchers, headless browsers, background shells) when it ends and names the worktrees other or earlier sessions left in the project, never removing one; report mode until SESSION_CLEANUP=on.
rules: Never touches a process it did not start, and never removes a worktree: it only names them.
Windows only; elsewhere it does nothing.

nodes.name: Systems map hooks
nodes.what: The hooks that give helpers the map lines, flag drifted links, refuse edits of generated files and ask for a map.
rules: map-generated is the only map hook that refuses (an edit of a file listed under generated); the others never block and fail open.

nodes.name: Systems map skill
nodes.what: The map.mjs reader and the SKILL.md that tells a worker how to build, check and settle a project's map.

nodes.name: Systems map graph panel
nodes.what: The Nimbalyst panel that draws the project's map as a graph with cards for each part.

nodes.name: Helper run log and Agents Panel
nodes.what: One line per helper into agent-runs.jsonl, read by the Agents Panel.
rules: Writes nothing to stdout, so it never touches the Agent input map-brief rewrites.
extensions/agents-panel/src/runs.js imports nothing: build.mjs inlines it into dist/index.js.
The panel never changes the app's own elements (the split's two heights aside): it adds only data-ap-* attributes and its own .ap-* elements.

nodes.name: Plan usage log and dashboard
nodes.what: Plan-percentage samples, the usage-plan panel, the usage dashboard and its trigger word.
rules: The saved login is sent only to api.anthropic.com and never written to the log.
Sessions never wait for the request: the hook checks a timestamp and starts a detached --fetch copy.
Inside Nimbalyst the dashboard hook never opens a browser: it refreshes the data and names the click.

nodes.name: Setup audit scanners
nodes.what: The setup-audit skill: scripts that read chats and usage and write the audit, with their own small libraries.
rules: review-scan calls no model and sends nothing anywhere.

nodes.name: Session handoff
nodes.what: Writes a short brief of a session so work continues in a fresh one; the session comes from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (or --session), and the brief is built from that session's own transcript and summary.
rules: The brief comes only from this session's own transcript, never another session's file: two chats in one folder can hand off in the same minute.
No summary file, no brief: an empty summary leaves the next session to guess.

nodes.name: Steer and self-compact
nodes.what: Mid-turn steering of a session and the compact of itself, driven by hooks. The note asks for the mid-turn notes to be listed back under "### Your notes" and says when a note waited 2 min or more.
rules: A note counts as delivered only once its [note id] marker is in the session's transcript.
/compact never lands in a busy session: compact-self waits for the turn to end.

nodes.name: Phone bot
nodes.what: The phone app's PC program and its join skill: a Telegram Mini App drives Nimbalyst sessions through a relay.
rules: Every call to Nimbalyst's local MCP endpoint lives only in bot/nimbalyst.mjs; its token is never written, logged or put in an error message.
The scheduled task of earlier versions is only deleted, never made (Windows Defender flagged it).

nodes.name: Setup update and release
nodes.what: Version check on prompt (and the background self-install of a release that asks nothing, files-only or quiet), the update-setup skill that installs a newer release, the tidy of the person's own rules, and the version and changelog files.
rules: The version check never downloads or installs anything itself; the self-install runs detached, so the prompt never waits.
Only a release that needs the person's answer waits for /update-setup; every other one installs itself.
An update never asks what is already set up or answered, and opens no project window.
version.json is written by scripts with JSON.stringify: never format it by hand (Biome leaves it out).
skills/update-setup/update.mjs is left out of the formatter: the privacy word list allows a word on one line number.

nodes.name: Project update pass
nodes.what: /update-project brings one project folder up to the current setup, every change shown first, and stamps the folder as done at the pass level.
rules: The pass level (LEVEL in pass.mjs, projectPass in version.json) goes up only with a release that changes what a project folder should hold.
The gh calls of checks P20-P22 and P26 are GETs only.

nodes.name: Installer core
nodes.what: install.mjs and its steps: the file helpers, the repo sources and the setup state it remembers.
rules: A file the person changed is theirs: an update replaces a hook, skill, rules file or a folder's CLAUDE.md only while it is exactly what an earlier run wrote.
profile.md and finds/INDEX.md are written only when missing.
A replaced file is kept first in ~/.claude/setup-logs/<date>-install-backup/.

nodes.name: Hook wiring
nodes.what: Puts the hooks of settings.example.json into the user's settings and takes retired ones out.
rules: settings.example.json is the one hook table; its _setup key is never written into a settings.json.
A new hook is wired in settings.example.json (or a group of hooks/dispatch-groups.json) and covered by tests/test-wiring.mjs.
A retired entry with arguments unwires only that exact entry: repeat-guard.mjs takes the bare entry and leaves repeat-guard.mjs --near-cap-only.

nodes.name: Hook dispatcher
nodes.what: Runs one group of hooks (pre-tool, prompt, stop) in one Node process and joins their answers into one.
rules: A file is listed once per group: Node runs a module once per process, so a second entry of it does nothing.
A guard (guard: true) that throws, exits non-zero, cannot load or runs out of time stops the call; any other hook is crash-logged and the rest still run.
DISPATCH=off ends every group at once, the guards included.

nodes.name: Claude home files and rules
nodes.what: Copies hooks, agents, skills and workers into the Claude home folder, merges the rules into CLAUDE.md and sets the model.
rules: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is replaced only when the person never changed it; the person's own rules move to rules/my-rules.md.

nodes.name: Project templates
nodes.what: Starter projects the installer places in the user's folders (claude-settings, quick-tasks), and the retired folders an update merges into quick-tasks.

nodes.name: Nimbalyst install steps
nodes.what: Finds Nimbalyst, builds and installs the extensions, sets the theme, plugins and app settings.
rules: A build never goes into Nimbalyst's extension folders: it goes to extensions-pending and is swapped in only while Nimbalyst is closed.
Nimbalyst's settings file is written only while Nimbalyst is closed: it rewrites the file from memory.
A theme the person picked stays.

nodes.name: Nimbalyst patcher
nodes.what: Puts the setup's fixes into Nimbalyst's app.asar and takes them out again; pin.json pins the Nimbalyst version the setup delivers, deliver.mjs downloads, installs and patches it, restart.mjs closes, installs, patches and reopens it.
rules: updater-block is requiredFirst and never retires: when it is skipped no patch is applied, or the next Nimbalyst update would wipe every fix.
All edits of a patch apply together or not at all, and each anchor must occur exactly once, else the patch is SKIPPED.
A replace text must never occur in the unpatched file: its presence is what marks the patch applied.
Only packed files change: an entry in app.asar.unpacked is never touched.
deliver.mjs installs and swaps panels only while Nimbalyst is closed (--install-now, --after-quit), never while it runs.
The quit listener never runs process.execPath (that is Nimbalyst.exe) and never holds up the app's quit.

nodes.name: Worker and reviewer agents
nodes.what: The agent definitions the main session hands work to, and the version checker worker.
rules: An agent file's frontmatter must be valid YAML: Claude Code drops a bad one without a word (tests/test-agents.mjs).
versions.mjs: a NO means only not in this list, never that the version does not exist.

nodes.name: Quick tasks project
nodes.what: The side-work folder for questions, finding things online and one-off file jobs: the finder skill and its link gate, and tools/peek.mjs, which reads pages in Nimbalyst's browser and with --save keeps each page's whole text in a file.

nodes.name: Web research skills
nodes.what: Skills for web research (the page-reading ladder, cheapest step first) and signed-in sites.

nodes.name: Page reader
nodes.what: workers/read-page.mjs saves the exact words of web pages as markdown files and says what read each one: Firecrawl Local first when it is installed (its cloud hand-off for pages that block it), defuddle otherwise. Exit 0 all read, 1 a page failed, 2 a usage error.
rules: A host that is or resolves to a private or local address is refused before any reader runs.
Firecrawl Local always runs with --public-only and never its init; defuddle is pinned at 0.19.7 and runs in an empty folder of its own.

nodes.name: PC tidy
nodes.what: Shows and frees memory held by finished sessions.
rules: Never stops Nimbalyst, the Nimbalyst delivery, the phone app's PC program, a terminal, ssh or gpg agents, a visible browser, or anything whose starter still runs.
An orphaned node or python it does not know is listed as MAYBE WANTED, never stopped.

nodes.name: Disk tidy
nodes.what: Report-first disk cleanup: leftover worktrees, old chat logs, scratch and temp folders, old project copies; the 60-day chat archive and its restore.
rules: Acts only on what the report listed; the person's own items only with their yes, item by item.
Never passes --force to git, never removes a dirty worktree or one with commits not on main, never removes ~/.claude/scratch, never writes a Nimbalyst file.

nodes.name: File upkeep
nodes.what: The file standard (names, places, decisions archive) and the checker that lists misnamed and misplaced files, with the reorganize ledger and undo.
rules: Only files git shows are read: git-ignored data is never flagged, moved or deleted.

nodes.name: Session board cleanup
nodes.what: Archives finished sessions on the Nimbalyst board.
rules: Pinned sessions are never archived and nothing is deleted; pick.mjs reads Nimbalyst's database read-only.

nodes.name: Workflow skills
nodes.what: Planning and design skills: lead, next-move, btw, new-project, design-system, untangle.
rules: leftover-worktrees.mjs never lists the main checkout and never touches a locked worktree or the one with the base branch; --remove takes only merged and clean ones.

nodes.name: Extension shared build
nodes.what: Build helpers, design tokens and the host bridge the Nimbalyst extensions share.
rules: CSS is never run through the formatter: tests read it as text and match the hand layout.
extensions/shared/orbs/orbs.js is a generated, minified bundle: Biome leaves it out entirely.

nodes.name: Commands extension
nodes.what: Slash command finder and composer inside Nimbalyst.
rules: A button only starts a new session: the app has no call into a running one, so /handoff and /btw are not buttons.
A button for a skill that exists only on this computer goes in own.ts, which the shared build (build:share) leaves out.

nodes.name: Read-aloud extension
nodes.what: Reads replies aloud with a local voice model.
rules: Built only with --with read-aloud or where it is installed already: it needs a speech program of its own.

nodes.name: Ink themes
nodes.what: Eleven colour themes added to Nimbalyst's theme list.
rules: extensions/ink-themes/manifest.json is written by a script with JSON.stringify: never format it by hand.
The themes may use !important: they must beat the host app's own CSS.

nodes.name: Test suite and privacy check
nodes.what: run-all with an empty home, the kit and the check that nothing private ships.
rules: Every test file runs with an empty home folder, as on GitHub's runners: never lean on files installed in ~/.claude.
Build hook JSON in Node or in a file, never inside a shell string: the shell mangles backslashes.
Run Biome pinned (npx @biomejs/biome@2.6.7), never a bare npx biome.
Real names belong in the privacy word list, never in privacy-check.mjs itself.

nodes.name: Blind reviewer agent
nodes.what: A reviewer that sees only what a person will see (screenshots, text, command output, docs), never the code or the chat, and ranks its flaws; it holds the screen checks of the retired blind-screen-review skill.
rules: Never sees the code or the chat: only what a person will see.

nodes.name: Video watching (/watch)
nodes.what: /watch turns a link or a video file into timed words and sheets of timed stills; with no subtitles, or when YouTube refuses them, it turns the sound into text on the computer (ffmpeg's whisper filter, else faster-whisper), long audio in pieces side by side.

nodes.name: Install opt-ins (voice typing, backup)
nodes.what: The first install's chat asks once about voice typing with Handy and the encrypted backup; install.mjs --handy and --backup only keep the answers in setup-state.json, and an update never asks voice typing again and asks the backup only while no answer is on record.
rules: install.mjs --handy and --backup only record the answers; the asking is the first install's chat.
An update never asks voice typing, and asks the backup only while no answer is on record.

nodes.name: Backup (/backup)
nodes.what: Encrypted restic backup (pinned 0.19.1) of the Claude folder and picked project folders to the person's own Backblaze B2 storage, set up with a key that can't delete; runs when asked or daily or weekly, with a restore test before the schedule starts and monthly, and restores into a new folder.
rules: A restore goes into a new folder, never over the original.
The restic password reaches restic only as RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE and the B2 key only as env vars: never on a command line or printed.

nodes.name: Verify skill templates
nodes.what: The four verify skill templates (web app, Godot game, command-line or Node tool, data or video pipeline) that /new-project writes and /update-project offers: how to start the app, what to do in it, what proof to show.

nodes.name: Log-only mode log printer
nodes.what: Prints what hooks in log-only mode (observe) would have refused, and each code commit verify-gate's commit check looked at, from hooks/state/observe.jsonl.

links.says: The Stop hooks run inside the same frame and read its state.
The map hooks use the frame and state for their hourly limits.
The command hooks run inside the frame.
The fence runs inside the frame and tells an app run from the terminal with its inNimbalyst.
Gate messages come from texts.mjs and scanners match them.
The audit scanners match the strings hooks write.
links.why: texts.mjs is the one home of each such text, so a reworded hook message cannot leave a scanner counting nothing.

links.says: The Stop hooks read the transcript through the shared reader.
planner-readonly keeps the reviewer and plan-reviewer to a read-only shell.
The hooks import map.mjs for the brief lines, the drift list and the file counts.
map-brief appends the map lines of the things a helper's brief names by file.
map-brief builds the helper brief through serves.mjs fullBrief.
The panel reads the same map file the skill checks.
links.why: The panel keeps its own copy of MAP_REL in map.ts, so moving the map file means changing both.

links.says: The map scan counts code through verify-gate's shared code-file list.
links.why: code-files.mjs is the one list of what counts as code, so the map's code count and verify-gate agree.

links.says: Logs each helper's type, model and effort.
The panel is built with the shared build helpers.
The audit and dashboard read the saved plan samples.
The usage-plan panel uses the shared build helpers.
The handoff brief reads only the transcript.
links.why: Two chats in one folder can hand off in the same minute, so the brief trusts only this session's own transcript.

links.says: steer is wired as a hook from the example settings.
The wakeup-note patch sends a wakeup that fires mid-turn with `steer.mjs send --to <id> - --nowait`, the text on stdin: exit 0 is a note, any other end queues the wakeup.
links.why: steer's hook labels every note as one the user sent, so the patch starts the note with a line naming it the session's own wakeup; a change to that label or to send's exit codes changes what the patch does.

links.says: The bot starts sessions through Nimbalyst.
An update re-runs the installer and compares versions.
After a setup install the update starts deliver.mjs --stage and says its status in grey lines; /update-setup's restart card runs restart.mjs.
links.why: Nimbalyst's own updater is off (updater-block), so the setup's update is the only way a new Nimbalyst arrives.

links.says: The uninstall puts Nimbalyst's original app.asar back through patch.mjs's restore, or prints the command when Nimbalyst runs.
links.why: patch.mjs does not export paths(), so uninstall.mjs repeats its resources folder layout: a layout change in patch.mjs needs uninstall.mjs changed too.

links.says: The update takes this version's rules and files; the person's own rules move to rules/my-rules.md.
links.why: The person's own rules must survive an update.

links.says: The installer wires hooks through wiring.mjs.
The installer copies the setup files and merges the rules.
The installer places the starter projects.
The installer builds extensions and sets Nimbalyst up.
Each wired hook is a file in hooks/ that runs in the frame.
Copies the agents and workers into the Claude home folder.
quick-tasks is one of the placed templates; an update copies the notes of the retired ask-anything and internet-search folders into it and leaves those folders.
The read-only browser hook protects the tools this project drives.
links.why: The browser CLI works in the person's signed-in accounts, so only read commands may pass.

links.says: The site login skill runs browser commands the guards check.
The installer builds the extensions that share the build helpers.
Lead hands steps to worker agents.
Extensions share tokens and the host bridge.
Same shared build and host.
The theme step picks the default ink theme.
Hook tests run each hook with an empty home.
The privacy check blocks private text in shipped files.
links.why: The repo is public: whatever a shipped file holds goes out to everyone.

links.says: The Nimbalyst tool gates run inside the hook frame.
An update cleans the setup's own leftovers and passes on the offer for the person's own.
An update passes on the file reorganize offer from the checker.
repeat-guard warns each helper agent near its turn cap, by the cap in its agent file.
The version check offers the pass in a folder behind its level, and an update says how many folders are behind.
disk-tidy offers the video-cache entries /watch left unused for 30 days; they are rebuilt on use.
The reading ladder sends a signed-in or script-built page to quick-tasks' peek.mjs.
The reading ladder saves a page a quote or a decision rests on with read-page.mjs, and a worker reads the file.
The skill says /deep-research runs only from the terminal; the fence refuses it elsewhere.
When Nimbalyst's browser can't be reached, peek.mjs stops and names read-page.mjs for a public page; the finder and read-web skills read public pages with it.
The answers reach install.mjs as --handy and --backup and are kept in setup-state.json for later runs.
A yes to the backup runs /backup as the full install's last step.
An update never asks voice typing (a Handy found on the computer goes on record as yes) and says one Backup line, asking the backup once while no answer is on record.
links.why: An update asks nothing that is already set up or answered.

links.says: backup.mjs reads setup-state.json for the Node path its schedule runs and the projects folder it lists.
The commit check writes one log line per checked code commit; observe-log prints it with its verdict.
hook-io's observe mode appends to observe.jsonl, which observe-log reads.
A load of the project's verify skill counts as a run, and the commit check runs only in a project that has one.
/new-project copies a template into .claude/skills/verify.
Check P27 offers a verify skill from the templates to a folder with code and none.
A helper a note stopped starts its report with "Stopped early for a user note:"; helper-stopped reads that line and has the session answer the user first.
links.why: steer.mjs writes the marker as its own literal, not from texts.mjs, so a reworded marker on either side stops helper-stopped from seeing a note stop.

evidence.token: Stopped early for a user note:

links.says: A dispatch.mjs entry in the settings counts every hook of its group as wired on that event.
The pre-tool group runs the shell guards in order, and an updatedInput goes on to the next hooks' event.
links.why: download-guard is listed before command-explain so its rewritten command still gets the explanation check.

links.says: The pre-tool group runs workflow-fence as a guard for Workflow calls only.
Each hook runs in the one process as if it were the script being run; process.exit ends only that hook (HookExit in hook-io.mjs).
